title: Príncipe v1.0.0
summary: The first stable release is tagged and the version is now visible in the app.
body: v1.0.0 is now the named release. You'll see the version number on the launch splash and in the About footer — both linked to the release notes on GitHub. Single-sourced from `package.json` and the git tag, so it stays in sync automatically.
why: Drafted from a recent product change.

title: PDF exports now match what you see on screen
summary: Ranked objections, blind spot, contested flag, and fixed text formatting all land in the exported report.
body: The PDF was lagging the UI — it showed a single objection and printed `*emphasis*` as literal asterisks. Now the export renders the top-3 ranked objections, the 'What the panel almost missed' blind spot, and the Contested minority-stronger flag. Single- and double-asterisk emphasis both render as bold, matching the on-screen cards.
why: Drafted from a recent product change.

title: Synthesis upgraded to Sonnet — reports hit harder
summary: The narrative pass (executive summary, pros/cons, insights) now runs on Claude Sonnet and is tuned for directness.
body: The synthesis model that writes the decision report's narrative has been upgraded and prompted for more direct, impactful prose. The change affects both the in-app result and the PDF export identically. No action needed — your next run will reflect the updated output.
why: Drafted from a recent product change.

title: Two security fixes: SSRF bypass + project privilege escalation
summary: An IPv6-mapped SSRF bypass and a horizontal privilege-escalation path across projects are both patched.
body: The SSRF filter was missing IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses (e.g. `::ffff:127.0.0.1`), allowing a bypass of the private-IP block. Separately, a missing ownership check let a user read another project's data by manipulating request parameters. Both are fixed in this release. The member-invite feature has also been removed to eliminate an invite-token account-takeover vector until a proper design is in place.
why: Drafted from a recent product change.

title: Your panel now updates itself daily
summary: A signed cyber-news feed refreshes the panel daily, so every persona reacts to this week's breaches, regulation, and vendor moves.
body: Each CISO is grounded in the world that touches their seat. A daily pipeline scrapes public security sources, digests them (key points, never verbatim), signs the bundle, and your instance verifies and applies it — tagged by region and industry so the right personas react to the right news.
why: Major capability that isn't announced in the news center yet.
